title: Pullback of the quotient by an ideal
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, $f^*$ the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] and $\mathcal I=\mathcal J\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of the composite $f^*\mathcal J\to f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] (Stacks writes $f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$: the ideal sheaf generated by $f^\sharp(f^{-1}\mathcal J)$). Products $\mathcal K\mathcal F$ of a quasi-coherent ideal and a module, the powers $\mathcal K^n$ and the quotients $\mathcal F/\mathcal K\mathcal F$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). Then: (1) $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$, and for affine opens $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, $\mathcal I(U)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ generated by the image of $\mathcal J(V)$ under $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$; (2) for every $n\ge1$, $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^n$; (3) for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with quotient map $q_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G$, the morphism $f^*q_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\mathcal I\cdot f^*\mathcal G$; hence, with $p_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I f^*\mathcal G$ the quotient map, there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\sigma_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I f^*\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ with $\sigma_{\mathcal G}\circ p_{\mathcal G}=f^*q_{\mathcal G}$, and it is natural in $\mathcal G$: for every $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ between quasi-coherent modules, with induced maps $\bar u:\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'/\mathcal J\mathcal G'$ and $\overline{f^*u}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal If^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G'/\mathcal If^*\mathcal G'$, one has $\sigma_{\mathcal G'}\circ\overline{f^*u}=f^*(\bar u)\circ\sigma_{\mathcal G}$.

proof.text: Clause (1) is exactly the attached source theorem Scheme.IdealSheafData.ideal_comap_appLE, applied to J, f, V, U and hUV.

For clause (2), use affine opens U of X lying over affine opens V of Y. They cover X: choose an affine neighborhood V of f(x), then an affine neighborhood U of x inside its preimage. On each such U, apply the affine ideal formula to J and J^n. The formula ideal_pow and the ring identity Ideal.map_pow make the two ideals equal. Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext_of_iSup_eq_top glues the equality on this cover.

Let T = tensorPullback f, i_G be the inclusion JG -> G and k_G the inclusion (J.comap f)(TG) -> TG. Apply the image equality [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-product-image]. The inclusion k_G is mono because it is an image inclusion. Equality of the two subobjects gives an isomorphism of their domains commuting with the inclusions. Apply cokernel.mapIso, then cokernelImageι, then the inverse of PreservesCokernel.iso T i_G. T is a left adjoint by nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction, hence preserves cokernels and zero morphisms. This gives sigma_G: coker(k_G) -> T(coker(i_G)) as an isomorphism. The cokernel projection equations prove p_G >> sigma_G = T(q_G). Powers at one reduce definitionally to J and J.comap f, so these are precisely the requested quotients.

The projection p_G is epi, and the comparison sigma_G is an isomorphism, so T(q_G) is epi by its factorization. k_G >> T(q_G)=0 follows from the cokernel equation. Transport cokernelIsCokernel k_G across sigma_G using Cofork.ext and IsColimit.ofIsoColimit. Abelian.monoIsKernelOfCokernel then gives the requested limit kernel fork for k_G and T(q_G).

For u:G -> Gprime, the defining cokernel.desc equation gives q_G >> quotientMap(u) = u >> q_Gprime, and likewise on X. Precompose the desired naturality equality with p_G, use the factorization equations for sigma_G and sigma_Gprime, use T.map_comp and those two quotientMap equations, then cancel the epimorphism p_G. This is the Lean calc proof, with no remaining hole.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (all three clauses and the naturality clause checked; correct as stated). Tags 0887, 01AJ, 00DF, 01BG, 01I9, 01IA, 01IC, 01HV verified in tags/tags; the displayed computation in the proof of 0887 (coherent.tex 6643-6650) swaps the letters I and J (it writes f^{-1}I^n f^*G and G_{n+1}/I^nG_{n+1} for the ideal on Y). Proof written in six steps on the basis of affine opens U of X lying over affine opens V of Y: (1) from the image/cokernel node on affines, the pullback-quasi-coherent node, the structure-sheaf leaf (epsilon(f^*a)=f^sharp(a)) and a new node lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections ((f^*G)(U) = G(V) (x)_A B, natural in G; Schemes 01I9 with 01IA, as in Modules 01BG), giving I(U)=rho(J(V))B; (2) by the ring identity (rho(a)B)^n = rho(a^n)B and equality of quasi-coherent subsheaves on a basis; (3) the kernel of f^*q is computed on affines by right exactness of the tensor product (leaf 00DF) and the new node, then sigma is induced by the cokernel property and is an isomorphism because it is bijective on a basis (Mathlib leaf), whence f^*q is an epimorphism with kernel I f^*G; naturality by the epimorphism p. The node lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal (affine-base case) was not used: it is unsplit and narrower. One new node (unsplit, no Mathlib match after leansearch, leanfinder, loogle and grep).
